reason: The departing disk material has reached the cold cloud, so combining them should follow its destination directly.
expectation: I expect the disk material to mix with or change the cold cloud, though its ultimate fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The tail stars may change the surrounding gas, but I want to trace the disk material first.

effect: The disk material joined a cold cloud, completing its goal; I can now follow how young stars change their surroundings.
reaction: It is satisfying that grains missed by the planets can survive and join another cloud.
reason: The tail stars and their surrounding gas directly address the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the young stars to heat or illuminate some of the tail gas.

alternatives.reason: The nursery outflow may also change the cold cloud, but I will follow the tail stars first.

effect: The tail stars heat and sweep gas into a dense shell; the remaining offered combination follows the nursery outflow.
reaction: The expanding shell is a satisfying consequence of the stars' influence.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may show how the outflow changes the cold cloud.
expectation: I expect the outflow to heat, compress, or mix with the cloud, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The outflow's collision with the cloud formed new stars and completed the remaining goal.
reaction: I was surprised that a flow which cleared one nursery could help another gathering form stars.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the nursery outflow into the cold cloud was most worthwhile: it connected the earlier clearing to a new generation of stars.

leastWorthwhile.text: The tail-star combination was clear but comparatively predictable: the stars heated and swept up nearby gas.

surprise.text: The outflow helped trigger star formation after the shocked gas cooled, rather than simply dispersing the cloud.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless, although the last combination was the only offered action rather than a meaningful choice.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see how the surviving disk grains and newly formed stars affect later gatherings; those connected material histories held my interest.
